THE SCOPE HELPERS ARE SECURITY INVOKER AND app_authz IS UNTOUCHED. The obvious shape -- a sixth SECURITY DEFINER helper owned by app_authz -- is forbidden by the decision itself. NO HELPER BODY CALLS auth.uid(), AND THAT IS A MEASURED CONSTRAINT RATHER THAN A PREFERENCE. A `language sql` body is re-parsed in the calling session, so auth.uid() there is resolved as the CALLER and needs USAGE on schema auth -- which db/foundation/ci/supabase-shim.sql grants to nobody, and which no migration of ours can grant on the platform (011's header, measured: schema auth is owned by supabase_admin and postgres holds USAGE without grant option). The same call inside a POLICY is stored already resolved and needs only EXECUTE, which is why every policy in 010, 020 and 021 uses it and works. The identity therefore lives in the policy and the helpers read what that policy leaves them -- which is also why 021 writes no roster policy on the scope table.

The alternatives were to rewrite an applied migration -- forbidden -- or to add a policy that ANDs. Four `as restrictive` policies, one per batch 020 table, are the second; the version tables are included because a version row holds what a Business used to say and a narrowing that stopped at the current rows would leave an out-of-scope Business's history readable.

This increment writes an AUTH-3 table -- app.workspace_member_scopes says which Businesses and Pages a member's capability reaches -- and it is the first batch in this repository that NARROWS an existing grant rather than widening one. Both directions matter.

WHAT IT NARROWS: four RESTRICTIVE policies AND with batch 020's permissive ones, so a member holding a scope row reaches only the Businesses and Pages that row names, on the current tables and on the immutable version tables alike. A member holding no scope row is unaffected, which is the reading of §7 recorded in the manifest's blockers and asserted by cases in both directions; if the Product Owner wants absence to deny, that is an RFC and a data migration, not a predicate change.

WHAT IT WIDENS: §8.1's editor `P` on Business/Page INSERT/UPDATE/archive, conditioned on an EXPLICIT scope row. An unscoped editor gains nothing. Six permissive policies carry it and each also requires created_by = auth.uid() on INSERT and both halves on UPDATE; the page INSERT repeats batch 020's §11.3 archived-Business clause, because a permissive policy ORs and omitting it would have let a scoped editor do the one thing 020 wrote that policy to prevent.

THE ONE THING TO REVIEW HARDEST is that the scope helpers are SECURITY INVOKER. Their entire caller-only property rests on one policy -- `user_id = (select auth.uid()) and app.is_active_member(workspace_id)` -- and widening it fails OPEN rather than closed: a caller who could see a second member's scope rows would inherit whatever that member is scoped to, and a caller whose own rows were hidden would look unscoped and therefore unnarrowed. It is pinned character for character by a test, it is asserted live in both directions, and 021 deliberately writes NO roster policy on that table for this reason -- which costs an owner the ability to read another member's scope row back, recorded as an open item rather than absorbed.

Column-scoped grants throughout. No role -- client, service or app_authz -- holds UPDATE or DELETE on the scope table, asserted statically and again against the live ACLs at apply time, so a member scope can be created and not removed through the request path; §8.5 forbids a broad delete and names no lifecycle field for this row, so the field is not invented. `anon` is granted nothing, so an anonymous read is refused on the SCHEMA by the privilege system before RLS is reached. app_worker holds SELECT and INSERT and no policy, which is what makes RFC-2026-017 §7's service denial falsifiable on this table too. No secret, no PII and no customer content is written: every fixture id is uuid5 of its own symbol and the only new personal field is a display name reading "fixture page editor a". WHAT AN ABSENT SCOPE ROW MEANS IS A DECISION NO DOCUMENT MAKES. §7 fixes three scope types and says nothing about a member who holds none. 021 reads absence as NOT NARROWED: 010's own table comment already models scope as narrowing a ceiling and never widening it, and the fixture catalog describes user_owner_a and user_viewer_a with no scope at all, so the other reading would make `owner-a-sees-business-a1` false and would silently revoke Business access from every member nobody has scoped. The asymmetry that follows is the design and is asserted by cases in both directions: a `Y` operation is narrowed by scope where scope exists (member_scope_admits_*, true for an unscoped member) and a `P` operation requires an EXPLICIT scope (member_scope_covers_*, false for one). If the Product Owner wants absence to deny, that is an RFC and a data migration, not a predicate change.

A MEMBER SCOPE CAN BE CREATED AND NOT REMOVED THROUGH THE REQUEST PATH. §8.1's "Invite/change scope" is Y for owner and 021 writes the CREATE half. There is no UPDATE and no DELETE, for any role, because §8.5 forbids a broad user delete and requires a soft delete "ที่ update typed lifecycle field" and NO DOCUMENT NAMES A LIFECYCLE FIELD FOR THIS ROW. 010 could lean on §10 and §11.4 for an invitation's revoked_at; there is no equivalent sentence here, so the field is not invented. The refusal is at the PRIVILEGE layer and two cases assert it. Owed to whichever batch defines the lifecycle.

NO ROSTER READ ON THE SCOPE TABLE, so an owner may create a scope row for another member and may not read one back. §8.1's "Member list SELECT" is Y for owner and admin, and 011 implemented exactly that shape on app.workspace_members. It is not repeated here because the scope helpers resolve the caller from THIS table's own policy rather than by calling auth.uid() -- a `language sql` body is re-parsed in the calling session and would need USAGE on schema auth, which the CI shim grants to nobody and which no migration of ours can grant on the platform (011's header, measured) -- so a roster policy would widen what every helper sees. The two cannot both be had in this batch; the narrower one is taken. It also means an INSERT for another member cannot carry RETURNING, because Postgres applies SELECT policies to a returning clause.

THE POLICY THE BATCH RESTS ON IS PINNED AGAINST THE MIGRATION TEXT AND NOT AGAINST A DEPARSED CATALOG STRING. RFC-2026-020 §6.1/5 pins app_authz's policy by `pg_get_expr`, and that literal was DERIVED FROM A MEASUREMENT -- PostgreSQL 17.6's own deparser, read read-only off the provisioned instance. The text pin holds today and the catalog pin is owed to whoever first applies 021 somewhere a `pg_get_expr` can be read off.
